answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable stake before it can transact, like a toll at the single inlet to a shared orchard on a mesa: one agent, one bond, locked for a fixed window. New identities start in a low-trust tier and earn higher limits only through useful work attested by independent peers. If an identity is caught duplicating work or voting twice, its stake is slashed and its reputation is burned, so spinning up a hundred fake agents costs a hundred bonds while gaining no extra influence.
